content.comment_body: How can a true on-off delay be achieved so that, if the input signal disappears and returns during the off-delay period, the timer's on-delay will not restart? The standard on-off delay block resets the on-delay when the signal returns, but that's not the desired outcome.

One approach is to use two on-delay blocks. I included a few AND logic gates to handle timer resets and pulse generators to display a message during the delay period. The on and off delays are both set to 10 seconds. The display also shows configured and running timer values. Is it possible to use fewer or alternative logic blocks while keeping this functionality?

analysis.insight_summary: The user wants to build an accurate on-off delay timer using [company_name] automation logic blocks. The built-in on-off delay function restarts its on-delay timer when the input returns during off-delay, but the user needs the delay to continue uninterrupted. Their current method uses several on-delay blocks, logic gates, and pulse generators, but they're seeking a more efficient solution without losing the required behavior.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the on-off delay logic to complete the off-delay countdown regardless of input signal toggling. They also want to decrease the number of logic blocks used while maintaining all necessary functionality.
